messages:
Eva Chen: quick heads-up — after the nightly perf sweep i keep hitting OOMs on A100-80GB when paged-attn compaction runs mid-request. looks like a spike in workspace alloc + a kernel fallback. repro in the long-seq workload (~2k tokens).
Mike Patel: can you paste the profiler slice? curious whether compaction is doing synchronous H2D/D2H copies or starving the allocator. :thinking:
Eva Chen: profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
TIMELINE: allocate_workspace 00:00:01.234 allocate 3.2GB
TIMELINE: compaction_start 00:00:01.237 free_blocks=120 used_blocks=480 compaction_count=1
TIMELINE: memcpy H2D 00:00:01.238 1.5GB blocking
TIMELINE: kernel_launch 00:00:01.240 attn_optimized failed -> fallback attn_naive
TIMELINE: OOM 00:00:01.241
```
KV cache stats: total_blocks=600 block_size=8MB free_frag_ratio=0.28
Mike Patel: that memcpy looks bad. if compaction triggers big H2D moves we could blow the reserved ws and then the runtime picks a fallback kernel that needs more temp memory.
Rupert Lin: a few ideas — 1) lower compaction aggressiveness (threshold or target fill ratio), 2) reserve a small dedicated scratch (e.g. 512MB) for compaction so it never competes with per-request workspace, 3) prefer in-place block reuse for prefix reads instead of copying to new blocks.
Sophia Ramirez: also consider changing batching heuristics: if avg_seq_len > 1k, avoid running compaction synchronously during request handling; instead mark for background compaction between requests. we can gate that with a flag so dedicated pools can pick behavior.
Mike Patel: quick canary envs to try: REDWOOD_ALLOC_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=0.2 and REDWOOD_WS_RESERVED=536870912. that should cut compaction frequency and force reservation of 512MB. can you run one canary?
Eva Chen: ran the canary on the same workload. result: no hard OOMs, but 95th-tail latency increased ~7%. profiler now: compaction_count down from 3->1 per run, memcpy peaks reduced, but memcpy still happens earlier and causes a small latency spike (likely the reserved scratch memcpy).
Rupert Lin: expected tradeoff. the reservation avoids OOM but adds DMA overhead. We should optimize compaction algorithm: incremental compaction window that migrates small runs of blocks asynchronously and updates the blockmap atomically. example sketch:
```
for window in compaction_windows:
  gather_small_runs(window)
  async_copy(runs->scratch)
  atomic_swap_blockmap(runs)
  reclaim_scratch
```
This keeps single-copy sizes small so H2D bursts are smaller.
Sophia Ramirez: file a perf ticket? add telemetry metrics: compaction_duration_ms, memcpys_during_compaction, kernel_fallback_count, ws_alloc_hitrate. Also add a canary config for dedicated pools to set REDWOOD_WS_RESERVED automatically for long-seq models.
Mike Patel: i'll own the ticket and the canary rollout. please upload logs (profiler slices + env settings). i'll tag eng-sre if we need alloc infra changes. :thumbsup:
Eva Chen: uploaded logs to the thread and to s3:/redwood/perf/kv-compact/1802345678/ — includes raw perf traces, blockmap dumps, and the canary config used.
deploy-bot: canary applied to rc/kv-compact-tune-3 (rollout 10%)
Sophia Ramirez: thanks all — next actions: (1) mike files ticket + attach traces, (2) rupert prototype incremental compaction, (3) add telemetry, (4) run larger canary on dedicated pool.
Mike Patel: done — ticket ENG-RUNTIME-3421 created and assigned to me. tagging rupert for compaction PR.
Rupert Lin: i'll spike the incremental compaction this week and post microbenchmarks.
Eva Chen: great. leaving the canary running and collecting tail traces.
